title: ICC holds 4th pretrial meet in Duterte case
summary: The International Criminal Court is holding today the fourth status conference on former president Rodrigo Duterte’s crimes against humanity case.

blocks.text: Photos courtesy of the International Criminal Court show former president Rodrigo Duterte during his first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025.
MANILA, Philippines — The International Criminal Court (ICC) is holding today the fourth status conference on former president Rodrigo Duterte’s crimes against humanity case.
Commencing at 10 a.m. in The Hague, Netherlands (4 p.m. in Manila), the status conference will be livestreamed with a 30-minute delay.
Expected to be tackled are the trial schedule, including time allotted for opening statements and the first block of evidence to be presented in December.
Parties will discuss the prosecution’s witness list and number of hours to present the case, the estimated time needed by the defense and victims’ common legal representative.
He appeared at the Sept. 16 status conference.
No waiver of appearance has been publicly released.
The ICC Trial Chamber III has found Duterte fit to stand trial, which begins Nov. 30.
